source_guideline: WHO SMART Guidelines ANC / ANCDT01 (Danger Signs Triage)
entry_criteria: Pregnant woman presenting with severe headache, convulsions, vaginal bleeding, visual disturbances, or loss of consciousness
danger_signs: Convulsing
Severe headache with visual disturbance
Heavy vaginal bleeding
Unconscious or lethargic
mandated_actions: Immediate emergency stabilization (maintain airway, left lateral tilt, IV access)
Evaluate for immediate Magnesium Sulfate if eclamptic or pre-eclamptic convulsions
Immediate emergency transfer to Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmONC) facility
negative_boundaries: 🛑 NEVER delay emergency transfer for non-urgent routine antenatal profiling.
🛑 DO NOT administer oral sedatives (Diazepam) prior to airway protection and MgSO4 evaluation.

source_guideline: WHO SMART Guidelines ANC / ANCDT04 & ANCDT17 (Severe Pre-Eclampsia)
entry_criteria: Pregnant female >= 20 weeks gestation with SBP >= 160 mmHg or DBP >= 110 mmHg, or BP >= 140/90 with 2+ proteinuria or headache
danger_signs: Systolic BP >= 160 mmHg or Diastolic BP >= 110 mmHg
Proteinuria >= 2+ on dipstick
Epigastric pain or persistent visual scotomata
mandated_actions: Administer Magnesium Sulfate loading dose (4g IV over 15 min + 10g IM)
Initiate Oral Labetalol 200mg BD (or Methyldopa 250mg TDS / Nifedipine 10mg)
Urgent emergency transfer to CEmONC facility
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICTLY PROHIBIT ACE-Inhibitors (Enalapril) and ARBs (Losartan) -> Severe fetotoxicity and fatal fetal renal dysgenesis.

source_guideline: WHO SMART Guidelines ANC / ANCDT25 (Anaemia Counselling & Management)
entry_criteria: Pregnant woman with Hb < 110 g/L (1st/3rd trimester) or Hb < 105 g/L (2nd trimester) or severe clinical pallor
danger_signs: Severe anaemia with Hb < 70 g/L
Signs of cardiac failure or severe dyspnea
mandated_actions: Double elemental Iron therapy to 120mg daily + Folic Acid 400mcg daily
Co-treat underlying parasitic infection (deworming after 1st trimester; malaria test)
Recheck Hb in 4 weeks
negative_boundaries: 🛑 DO NOT take oral iron concurrently with tea, coffee, or calcium (separate by 2 hours).
🛑 If Hb < 70 g/L, DO NOT manage at Level 1 dispensary -> Urgent hospital referral for parenteral iron or transfusion.

source_guideline: WHO SMART Guidelines ANC / ANCDT27 (Pre-Eclampsia Risk Stratification)
entry_criteria: Pregnant woman >= 12 weeks gestation with high pre-eclampsia risk (prior pre-eclampsia, chronic HTN, diabetes, or twins)
danger_signs: New hypertension >= 140/90 after 20 weeks gestation
mandated_actions: Initiate Low-Dose Aspirin (75-150mg daily) starting at 12-20 weeks gestation until delivery
Co-prescribe Calcium carbonate 1.5-2.0g daily in low dietary calcium populations
negative_boundaries: 🛑 DO NOT initiate Low-Dose Aspirin prior to 12 weeks gestation.
🛑 DO NOT prescribe full-dose Aspirin (>300mg) or systemic NSAIDs in pregnancy (premature ductus arteriosus closure).

source_guideline: WHO SMART Guidelines ANC / ANCDT38 (Malaria Prophylaxis)
entry_criteria: Pregnant woman in malaria-endemic setting attending antenatal care from 2nd trimester (>=13 weeks)
danger_signs: Fever, rigors, positive malaria rapid test
mandated_actions: Administer Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP: 3 tablets stat) under DOT at each monthly visit starting in 2nd trimester
Screen concurrent medications at every antenatal contact
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give IPTp-SP if mother takes daily Co-trimoxazole for HIV -> Severe antifolate toxicity and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
🛑 DO NOT give IPTp-SP in first trimester (<13 weeks).

topic: Poliovirus: Live bOPV vs Inactivated IPV Contraindications
entry_criteria: Infant or child presenting for routine poliovirus vaccination (bOPV or IPV)
danger_signs: Severe immunocompromised status (symptomatic HIV, primary immunodeficiency)
Anaphylaxis history to neomycin, streptomycin, or polymyxin B
mandated_actions: Screen immune status prior to oral polio (bOPV) administration
Substitute oral live bOPV with Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) if severely immunocompromised
Record vaccine formulation administered in child health card
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give live bOPV to severely immunocompromised infants -> High risk of VAPP.
🛑 DO NOT vaccinate with IPV if history of anaphylaxis to streptomycin, neomycin, or polymyxin B.

entry_criteria: Infant presenting for routine Rotavirus vaccine schedule (6 and 10 weeks)
danger_signs: Prior history of intussusception or bowel obstruction
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) or symptomatic immunodeficiency
Acute severe vomiting, diarrhea, or acute febrile illness
mandated_actions: Screen infant for past intussusception or bowel abnormalities
Confirm immune competence prior to oral live rotavirus vaccine administration
Temporarily defer rotavirus administration during acute gastroenteritis
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give Rotavirus vaccine if infant has prior history of intussusception.
🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give Rotavirus vaccine in infants with SCID or severe immunodeficiency.

topic: BCG: Immunodeficiency & Maternal HIV Exposure Safety
entry_criteria: Newborn or infant eligible for BCG tuberculosis vaccination
danger_signs: Confirmed symptomatic HIV or severe congenital immunodeficiency
Systemic immunosuppressive therapy in infant or late pregnancy
Active systemic illness, generalized lymphadenopathy, or failure to thrive
mandated_actions: Screen maternal HIV status and infant clinical HIV staging prior to BCG
Give BCG at birth to asymptomatic HIV-exposed infants with early virological testing
Withhold BCG in infants with symptomatic HIV until confirmed immune reconstitution on ART
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give BCG if infant has symptomatic HIV or immunodeficiency -> Risk of fatal disseminated BCGitis.
🛑 DO NOT vaccinate with BCG during pregnancy or in infants under 1 year on immunosuppressants.

topic: Measles Live Vaccine: Severe Immunosuppression Safety
entry_criteria: Child eligible for routine Measles/MR vaccine (9 and 15-18 months)
danger_signs: Severe immunosuppression (advanced HIV/AIDS Stage 3-4, leukaemia, lymphoma)
History of severe anaphylactic reaction to neomycin or gelatin
Pregnancy
mandated_actions: Screen child for severe immunosuppressive disease or chemotherapy
Administer measles vaccine to HIV-infected children who are NOT severely immunosuppressed
Administer 0.5 mL subcutaneously once clearance confirmed
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give live Measles vaccine to severely immunosuppressed individuals (Stage 4 HIV, low CD4%).
🛑 CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT vaccinate pregnant women or individuals with severe anaphylaxis to neomycin or gelatin.
